name: Strid

attributes.attribute: a narrow pass in the River Wharfe at Bolton Abbey
goddess of the waterfall who rides a white horse
her appearance often presages death by drowning

sources: Clarke, David, with Andy Roberts. Twilight of the Celtic Gods: An Exploration of Britain’s Hidden Pagan Traditions. London: Blandford, 1996, 96+.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Strid is a British folkloric site. Near Bolton Abbey in West Yorkshire the river Wharfe runs through a narrow pass. That pass is the Strid. On the morning of Beltane a woman was said to rise there, riding a white horse. The local people held the rider to be Verbeia, a goddess of the water and the land. Her riding on such a morning was no friendly visit. Those who came to the river at that hour were warned to take care, for her show often foretold death by drowning. The tale gives the narrow rift a presence of its own in the old belief of the country.
